As of 146 AM Monday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1...  A surface cold front could bring a few isolated 
showers late this afternoon and evening. The main story, however, 
will be cooler temperatures.

A surface cold front will move through the region later tonight, 
roughly between 9 pm and midnight. Prior to that, we will start out 
the day with a low clouds and patchy fog. It may take some time for 
the low clouds to disperse, especially across the eastern portions 
of our forecast area. Regardless, mid/high clouds will stream in 
tied to a strong subtropical jet. Temperatures will be rather mild 
to start the week in the low 70s for most places. Ahead of the 
surface cold front, the HRRR/RRFS are indicating some weak surface-
based instability. This could aid some isolated to scattered rain or 
showers late this afternoon and early evening. Guidance shows 
activity tracking ESE from the Triad late this afternoon into the 
Sandhills tonight. Most areas will see light accumulation of rain, 
if any. Cannot rule out some patchy low clouds or fog in the east 
ahead of the front. Otherwise, much cooler behind the front in the 
40s, with much lower dewpoints.

KEY MESSAGE 2... A potent storm system will affect much of the 
eastern United States including our region beginning Wednesday and 
lasting into Thanksgiving Day. Chilly temperatures, gusty NE wind, 
and heavy rain should all target Wednesday afternoon into 
Thanksgiving morning. Rainfall of 2-3 inches, gusty wind to 35 mph, 
and chilly temperatures are expected. 

We realize this is a huge travel period Wednesday and Wednesday 
night. If the winds and rain verify, there will be plenty of water 
on the roadways and some urban and low lying areas will have minor 
flooding. This will lead to increased hydroplaning potential making 
driving hazardous. The winds could also down small limbs creating 
some road hazards, as well. 

Tuesday will be the dry and chilly day before the heavy rain and 
gusty wind mid-week.

Models continue to trend toward a potent storm system that will 
affect areas MS/AL north and east along all the eastern United 
States Wednesday through Thanksgiving Day. We will likely begin the 
system Wednesday with a chilly morning thanks to a strong dry air 
ridge (DAR) (surface pressures 1040+ mb over the Great Lakes to NE 
states) will be extending down the eastern seaboard into NC/SC/GA. 
Lows will be in the 30s. The dry and cold air near the surface will 
be overridden by increasing warm air advection well above the 
surface Wednesday morning leading to increasing clouds. The clouds 
will likely keep the temperatures in check as rain develops and 
overspreads NC from the south during the morning. Temps should 
slowly reach the 40s to mid 50s north to south by afternoon before 
falling during the afternoon, especially as rain falls through the 
strong DAR. Wet bulbing as the rain increases in intensity during 
the afternoon will lead to highs holding in the 40s west and 50s 
east.

As the mid/upper level trough continues to strengthen and approach 
the TN Valley and southern Appalachians, our region will experience 
NE winds increasing to 15-25 mph with gusts to 30-35 mph as the 
pressure gradient increases Wednesday night. This occurs as the CAD 
strongly develops with the diabatic cooling in the Piedmont keeping 
high pressure in place there, and low pressure develops to our 
south. The low pressure is expected to track NNE either along the 
coast or just inland from the coast into eastern NC Thanksgiving 
morning. As this occurs, rain will be widespread and locally heavy. 
The heaviest rain is expected closer to the coast where a thermal 
moisture boundary develops along the slowly retreating inland CAD. 
Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are initially expected, with 2-3 
inches in the east. Any significant flooding is not likely due to the 
dry weather of recent weeks. 

The low pressure should track over the eastern areas by noon 
Thanksgiving, with the CAD holding in west characterized by 
lingering rain, drizzle, and fog with temperatures in the 40s 
Wednesday night and Thursday morning. Temperatures in the east will 
rise into the 60s as the warm front/TMB, and low pressure storm pass 
overhead and then north into eastern VA. There may be a few strong 
storms near the coast early Thursday if the low tracks far enough 
west allowing for unstable air to move a bit inland. For now, we 
placed a chance of thunder in our Coastal Plain Thursday morning. 

Otherwise, the system will move on north Thursday night and Friday. 
There will be some gradient winds behind the system, strongest in 
the Foothills into the Triad and NW Piedmont. Otherwise, clearing 
and rather mild conditions are expected late Thursday into Friday.
